title: Glasses or Something Else?

patient.name: Mr Koh Teck Huat
patient.presenting_complaint: Follow-up visit — gradual painless reduction of vision in the right eye over several months

history.hpc: Mr Koh has noticed his right eye vision has become progressively dimmer and hazier over the past 6 months, like looking through a 'foggy window'. His left eye vision feels unchanged. He has no pain, redness, or flashes/floaters. He last changed his glasses about 3 years ago. He has come in for a follow-up visit and visual acuity testing with pinhole has been ordered to help differentiate the cause of his reduced vision.
history.pmhx: Hypertension. No previous eye surgery. Known early cataract right eye noted at last visit 8 months ago.
history.family_hx: Mother had cataract surgery in both eyes in her 70s
history.social_hx: Retired bus driver. Wears distance glasses, prescription last updated 3 years ago.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye: moderate nuclear sclerotic cataract, increased compared to 8 months ago. Left eye: mild nuclear sclerosis, stable.
examination_findings.fundus: Right eye: hazy view due to cataract, no obvious posterior pathology seen. Left eye: normal.

pinhole_test.method: Pinhole occluder placed over current spectacle correction for each eye in turn, right eye tested first
pinhole_test.result: Right eye shows NO improvement with pinhole — suggests reduced vision is NOT primarily refractive, consistent with the known progressing cataract. Left eye shows mild improvement with pinhole — suggests a small residual refractive component.

investigations.va_summary: RE: 6/24 unaided/with glasses, no improvement with pinhole. LE: 6/9 with glasses, improves to 6/6 with pinhole.

diagnosis: Pinhole testing completed for both eyes. Right eye vision does not improve with pinhole, consistent with the known progressing nuclear cataract as the cause of reduced vision rather than a change in refractive error. Left eye shows mild improvement with pinhole, suggesting a minor refractive update may help. For doctor's review regarding cataract surgery referral for the right eye.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and confirm current spectacles are being worn for the test
Perform hand hygiene and wipe occluders (including pinhole occluder) with alcohol wipes before starting
Measure VA with current glasses for each eye first (right eye first by convention), occluding the other eye
For any eye with VA of 6/12 or worse, place the pinhole occluder over the current spectacle correction and retest that eye
Document whether vision improves, stays the same, or worsens with pinhole for each eye
Compare today's findings with the cataract findings noted 8 months ago to assess progression
Wipe occluders with alcohol wipes after the test and perform hand hygiene
Document all VA and pinhole results clearly and pass to doctor along with the anterior segment findings
follow_up: Doctor to review pinhole results alongside cataract grading and decide if right eye cataract surgery referral is appropriate
Left eye may benefit from updated refraction given mild pinhole improvement
Patient to be scheduled for biometry if cataract surgery is being considered for the right eye
patient_education: Explain that the pinhole test helps the doctor understand whether his blurry vision could be improved with new glasses or whether it is due to the cataract
Explain that since the right eye does not improve with the pinhole, his cataract is likely the main cause of the haziness he describes
Reassure patient that cataract surgery is a common and generally successful procedure if the doctor recommends it

key_points: Confirms patient identity and confirms current glasses are worn for testing
Elicits the gradual, painless nature of the visual decline and absence of red flag symptoms (no flashes/floaters/pain)
Reviews previous documented findings (known early cataract 8 months ago) for comparison
Performs hand hygiene and wipes occluders with alcohol wipes before starting
Measures VA with current correction for each eye, right eye first, with correct occlusion technique
Applies pinhole correctly only to eyes with VA 6/12 or worse (or as per protocol) and documents the result
Clearly documents whether pinhole improves, does not change, or worsens vision for each eye
Compares results with prior visit findings to assess for progression
Correctly interprets no improvement with pinhole in the right eye as suggesting a non-refractive cause (consistent with progressing cataract)
Correctly interprets improvement with pinhole in the left eye as suggesting a refractive component
Does not diagnose the final cause independently — presents pinhole findings alongside anterior segment findings to doctor
Recognises the value of comparing serial findings over time to track cataract progression
Documents VA and pinhole results accurately and clearly for both eyes
Hands findings to doctor with relevant context (known cataract, prior visit comparison)
Educates patient on what the pinhole result suggests in plain language
Provides reassurance regarding cataract surgery as a common and generally successful procedure
